new_entities.name: Hepatitis B vaccination at birth
new_entities.description: Hepatitis B vaccination begun at birth as part of universal infant immunization.

new_entities.name: Childhood and young-adult hepatocellular carcinoma
new_entities.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma arising from childhood through young adulthood.

edges.effect_quant: The Taiwan registry data show a durable and substantial reduction in hepatocellular carcinoma after universal infant hepatitis B immunization, with relative risks around one-third to two-fifths of the unvaccinated rate through childhood and young adulthood.
edges.population: birth cohorts receiving universal hepatitis B vaccination beginning in infancy, including a birth dose
edges.mechanism: Birth-dose hepatitis B vaccination prevents perinatal and early-life HBV infection, which is the critical upstream driver of chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, and later hepatocellular carcinoma in endemic settings. Because the vaccine blocks the carcinogenic infection itself, the cancer-prevention signal strengthens over time rather than disappearing.
edges.summary: This is a landmark prevention edge rather than a speculative association. The strongest Taiwan follow-up studies show that infant hepatitis B immunization sharply lowers hepatocellular carcinoma incidence from childhood into young adulthood, and the long-term cohort work makes clear that the residual failures occur disproportionately in incompletely immunized children and in those born to highly infectious mothers.
edges.caveats: The most dramatic evidence comes from Taiwan, where baseline HBV burden was high and nationwide follow-up was unusually strong, so absolute effect sizes may differ in lower-incidence settings. Even so, the causal chain is exceptionally coherent and the cancer-prevention effect is one of the best documented vaccine successes in chronic-disease prevention.

evidence.citation: ChangMH et al 2009 J Natl Cancer Inst
evidence.notes: Decreased incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in hepatitis B vaccinees: a 20-year follow-up study.

effect_quant.comparator: persons vaccinated at birth versus unvaccinated birth cohorts

evidence.notes: Long-term Effects of Hepatitis B Immunization of Infants in Preventing Liver Cancer.

effect_quant.comparator: vaccinated versus unvaccinated cohorts among 20- to 26-year-olds

evidence.notes: Incomplete hepatitis B immunization, maternal carrier status, and increased risk of liver diseases: a 20-year cohort study of 3.8 million vaccinees.
